name: SMT101x Sensors
description: Two modes for SMT101x tablets: recover the OEM publisher using your existing external MQTT settings, or manage sensors, switches, doors, and RGB backlight through Kiosk Satellite using the built-in local broker, with no separate MQTT server required.
author: Stuart Pearson

settings.title: Automatically re-enable disabled tablet MQTT
settings.description: With automatic recovery enabled, turns Android Settings > System > MQTT back on in either mode. Checks every minute, with a five-minute recovery cooldown; local mode waits for the broker. Reopen System settings to see the switch. Enabled does not guarantee delivery. Leave off to respect intentional disables. Server address, port, credentials, and client ID stay unchanged.

settings.title: Automatically recover stopped OEM MQTT publisher
settings.description: In either mode, checks every minute and restarts a stopped OEM publisher, with a five-minute recovery cooldown. Local mode waits for the broker. Does not repair a running but disconnected client or network/server failures, or verify external delivery. Disabled MQTT is respected unless automatic re-enabling is selected. Connection settings stay unchanged. See README for details.

settings.title: Host MQTT capture broker on this tablet
settings.description: On: sensors and controls through Kiosk Satellite, with no separate MQTT server. Set tablet MQTT to 127.0.0.1:1883; only local connections are accepted. Off: external MQTT recovery mode; keep your existing server settings and enable automatic recovery. External readings and controls are not bridged into Kiosk Satellite. This setting does not change the tablet's MQTT address.

settings.title: MQTT client ID (optional)
settings.description: Must match client_id in the tablet's MQTT settings, for example office. The OEM client uses this value as its MQTT topic prefix. Leave blank to learn it automatically from status publications.
